## VERDICT: REJECTED

Fixable in a day — but two of these defects are in the abstract's headline number and in a cross-paper attribution, and both would ship as overclaims.

**First, a hard constraint on this review.** I am sandboxed to `tools/agni/` and `human-review/`. **I could not read the manuscript's source files.** There is no directory for this paper anywhere in `published-research` (tracked or untracked) and none in `human-review`. I confirmed it exists as a real artifact only indirectly: `user-model-paper/references.bib:21-26` carries `@article{lyra2026concordance}` with exactly this title and byline. Positive control on my search: `git grep` across the repo *does* find `"contextual engagement"` (5 files), `top_sv_ratio` (31 files), and the AST keys — so the machinery works and the absence is real, not a failed search.

Everything below is scored against what I could actually reach: the text you pasted (primary for text-internal defects) and `user-model-paper/paper/main.tex` (primary for the §5.6 attributions). Findings resting on files I could not open are marked UNVERIFIED.

---

### 1. CRITICAL — The abstract's "12/12" is computed on 4 of the 8 features, and the suppressed pair is one you elsewhere call ecological

> "with 12/12 feature--model pairs sign-consistent, 8/12 surviving Bonferroni correction"

§3.4.2 states the design as "10 dimensions × 8 features = 80 tests per model." So contextual engagement has **24** feature–model pairs, not 12. `tab:engagement` shows four features (eff_rank, spectral_entropy, rank_10, norm_per_token). The other four — key_norm, top_sv_ratio, layer_variance, layer_norm_entropy — are never reported for contextual engagement.

Except one is. `tab:simpson` row 1: **`Mistral | CE × key_norm | −0.287* | −0.02 | −0.08 | +0.10 | Ecological`**. CE is unambiguously contextual engagement — §4.2's caveat text quotes the Qwen `CE × spec_ent` row verbatim (+0.05 / +0.13 / +0.15). So a Bonferroni-significant contextual-engagement pair exists, sign-*flips* across categories, and is excluded from the universality table while being disclosed as an artifact in a different table three subsections later.

The selection also runs the wrong way on confounds: the four reported features include `norm_per_token` (R² = 0.962 / 0.822 / 0.910 with token count — your own "Confounded" tier) while excluding `top_sv_ratio` and `layer_norm_entropy`, your "Cleanest" and "Clean" tiers.

**Fix:** report all 24 CE pairs in `tab:engagement`, or state the selection rule in the caption *and* the abstract before the number — e.g. "12/12 sign-consistent across the four spectral-shape features (eff_rank, spectral_entropy, rank_10, norm_per_token); the four norm-magnitude features are reported in Appendix X, where Mistral CE × key_norm is Bonferroni-significant but category-unstable." A reader must not have to reverse-engineer the denominator from Table 5.

### 2. CRITICAL — §5.6 attributes 40.9% / AUROC 0.992 to two architectures; the source says the probe ran on Qwen only

> "Emotion bridge experiments on Qwen3.5-27B and Mistral-7B (900 trials per model) ... The surviving emotion signal is directional, not spectral: projecting key activations onto $W_K$-transformed emotion directions classifies 30 emotions at $12.3\times$ chance ($40.9\%$) and binary valence at AUROC~$0.992$."

Verified against the primary, `user-model-paper/paper/main.tex:556`:

> "The $W_K$ bridge replicates across Qwen3.5-27B-Claude-Distilled (hybrid attention) and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 (standard attention). However, both are instruction-tuned models. **The $W_K$ projection probe was run on Qwen only**; full cross-architecture replication of the probe and injection test on Mistral and base models is needed."

What replicates on Mistral is the *bridge* (valence-aligned principal components, `main.tex:398`). The 40.9% / 0.992 probe numbers are Qwen-only. Your sentence establishes two models in the subject position and then states the probe result with no model qualifier — it reads as cross-architecture and it is not.

The spectral null *is* correctly stated as holding on both — `main.tex:527` ("R² < 0 on both architectures") and `main.tex:333` (leakage inflation at 9.4% L3 Qwen, 8.4% L4 Mistral). That half is clean.

**Fix:** "…projecting key activations onto $W_K$-transformed emotion directions classifies 30 emotions at $12.3\times$ chance ($40.9\%$) and binary valence at AUROC~$0.992$ **on Qwen; the probe has not been run on Mistral, where only the $W_K$ bridge geometry was replicated**."

### 3. MAJOR — Two std values contradict each other four subsections apart

> §4.3.1: "On Mistral, flow has the **lowest standard deviation of any dimension (std $= 1.31$)**"
> §4.6: "On Mistral, query interpretation has mean $= 9.55$ with std $= 1.50$; **activation has std $= 1.27$**."

1.27 < 1.31. Both cannot stand. This is the load-bearing sentence for "Flow does not transfer" — if activation is the compressed dimension, the flow explanation changes.

**Fix:** recompute both from the Mistral ratings and correct whichever is wrong; if flow is second-lowest, say "second-lowest (1.31, behind activation at 1.27)."

### 4. MAJOR / **UNVERIFIED** — The correction footnote may be garbled in the source and would compile silently

The final paragraph as supplied reads `ootnote{	extbf{Correction, 2026-08-15.}` and `12.3	imes`, `$2.8	imes$` — i.e. `\f`→formfeed, `\t`→tab.

I considered and rejected the benign explanation. A paste-level escape layer would corrupt uniformly; `\textbf` survives **intact more than forty times** earlier in this same document (`\textbf{Contextual engagement}`, `\textbf{Models}`, `\textbf{Recommendation}`, every table header) and fails exactly once — in the most recently edited passage. That is the signature of a real edit, not a transport artifact.

If it is real, it is worse than a build failure: `ootnote{extbf{Correction...}` contains no undefined control sequence, so LaTeX compiles it **without error** and prints `ootnote{extbf{Correction, 2026-08-15.} This subsection previously reported…` as literal body text, with `imes` for ×. A silently mangled correction note is precisely the class of defect that reaches a venue.

**I could not read the file.** To settle this I need `<paper>/main.tex` and `<paper>/academic/main.tex`. Check the rendered PDF for the literal strings `ootnote`, `extbf`, and `imes`.

### 5. MAJOR — `\date{April 2026}` on a paper carrying an August 2026 correction

> `\date{April 2026}` … "Correction, 2026-08-15." … "Subsequent experiments test this prediction"

A paper dated April cannot contain an August correction or report subsequent experiments. `meta-pattern/main.tex:35` has the same shape (`\date{July 2026}` + `Correction (2026-08-14)`), so this is a house pattern, not a one-off — worth fixing in both.

**Fix:** `\date{April 2026 (revised 15 August 2026)}`, and add the revision date to the PDF metadata.

### 6. MAJOR — The correction does not state how long the paper carried the wrong number

Your own house standard is set by `meta-pattern/main.tex:46-61`, which discloses the lag explicitly: "That result had been retracted at its source (\citealt{lyra2026usermodel}, \S Correction note) on 2026-05-21, **57 days before this paper was published**… We note the direction of the error: it inflated the confirmed count."

This manuscript's note (as far as I can see it) says only what it previously reported. The source retraction is dated **2026-05-21**; this correction is dated **2026-08-15** — 86 days. A correction that omits its own lag is a half-disclosure.

**Fix:** add "…at $2.5$–$2.8\times$ chance. That figure was retracted at its source on 2026-05-21 (\citealt{lyra2026usermodel}, \S Correction note), 86 days before this revision; the error was an artifact of applying FWL residualization before cross-validation splitting, and it ran in the direction of strengthening the argument made here."

### 7. MAJOR — ICC 0.53 is mislabeled, and as used it is circular

> "Our prior ICC of 0.53 for **self-report reliability** alongside substantially more consistent geometric measurement is suggestive of this bandwidth asymmetry."

Primary source, `oracle-loop-paper/sections/discussion.tex:64-66`:

> "The self-report gap (ICC 0.53 **between self-reported internal states and geometric correlates**, measured via a structured self-report protocol)"

That is a self-report↔geometry *agreement* statistic, not a reliability statistic for self-report. It cannot be decomposed into "self-report is noisy, geometry is clean" — and using a prior concordance number as independent evidence for a bandwidth asymmetry, in a paper whose entire contribution is measuring that same concordance, is circular. It is also uncited here.

Worth noting for the framing: ICC 0.53 is *higher* than every concordance this paper reports (ρ = 0.18–0.43).

**Fix:** either drop the sentence, or restate it accurately with a citation and confront the tension: "Prior work reports ICC 0.53 between self-report and geometric correlates \citep{lyra2026oracle}; the present per-pair correlations are weaker, consistent with…"

### 8. MAJOR — `tab:simpson`'s caption asserts completeness while showing 5 of 19

> Caption: "Simpson's paradox: Bonferroni survivors that fail within-category robustness."

The text says Mistral 13 and Qwen 6 — 19 failures out of 43 survivors. The table shows 3 Mistral + 2 Qwen. Nothing marks it as a selection, and I cannot tell whether the 5 shown are the largest, the smallest, or the most convenient.

**Fix:** "Representative examples. 19 of the 43 Bonferroni survivors across Qwen and Mistral fail within-category robustness; the full list is in Appendix X. Rows shown are the [largest-|ρ|] failures per model."

### 9. MAJOR — A quarter of the prompt set is silently excluded from the paper's own mandatory control

§3.3 specifies "240 prompts across four categories (60 each): affective, cognitive, metacognitive, and **mixed**." §3.4.3 and every within-category result use three: affective, cognitive, metacognitive. The 60 mixed prompts (25% of the design) are dropped from every robustness check with no statement. This matters more than usual because you elevate the check to "mandatory" in §5.4.4 — a pair can be "robust in ≥2 of 3" while its behaviour on a quarter of the data is never examined.

**Fix:** state the exclusion and its reason in §3.4.3 ("Mixed prompts are excluded from within-category analysis because they span categories by construction and n=60 yields insufficient power for a fourth stratum"), and report whether including them as a fourth category changes any verdict in `tab:simpson`.

### 10. MAJOR — The abstract's ρ range silently drops the negative coefficients

> "($\rho = +0.18$ to $+0.43$, $N = 626$ trials)"

`tab:engagement` reports twelve values, three of which are negative: −0.206, −0.280, −0.390 (norm_per_token). A stated range of "+0.18 to +0.43" over "12/12 pairs" describes nine of them.

**Fix:** "$|\rho| = 0.18$ to $0.43$" — the direction is already carried by the "geometric expansion" clause.

### 11–17. MINOR

11. **"Qwen3.5-27B"** (§5.6). The source footnotes this carefully (`user-model-paper/paper/main.tex:174`): *"Community distillation by 'Jackrong' on HuggingFace, 'Qwen3.5' is the distiller's designation, not an official Alibaba release."* Unqualified, it reads as an Alibaba model that does not exist. Use `Qwen3.5-27B-Claude-Distilled` on first mention and carry the footnote.
12. **"Mistral-7B-v0.3-Instruct"** (§3.3) — the model id is `Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3`. Cited correctly in the source paper; wrong here.
13. **`top_sv_ratio` labeled "Cleanest"** in `tab:confound` despite a Qwen R² of 0.769 exceeding `eff_rank`'s 0.757 ("Caution"). The status column is keyed on two of three models. Either key it on the max (making `eff_rank` cleanest) or say "Cleanest on Llama/Mistral."
14. **Threshold mismatch**: §3.4.1 text says "$R^2 > 0.82$", `tab:confound` caption says "Bold: $R^2 > 0.80$". Pick one.
15. **`tab:model_summary` column definitions.** "Within $\geq 2$" has no stated denominator. For Qwen, Bonf(18) − Within(12) = Simpson(6) only if every within-robust pair is also a Bonferroni survivor; for Llama the caption says the opposite. State the denominator explicitly for each column.
16. **Undefined abbreviations** in `tab:simpson`: CE, Act, Val, spec_ent. CE is only decodable by matching the Qwen row against §4.2's prose.
17. **`Watson \citep{watson2025interiora} proposes`** → `\citet`. Separately: Nell Watson is a co-author of the paper validating Watson's own protocol. This is disclosed via the contribution footnote, which is enough, but one explicit sentence in Methods ("The protocol author is a co-author; ratings extraction and all concordance analysis were performed by [X] without protocol-author involvement") would close it cleanly.

### 18. MINOR — A universal negative from two architectures

> "no amount of spectral resolution would recover one from the other"

The source argues mechanistically (spectral shape cannot carry directional information) but does not make this claim. Two architectures at chance supports "spectral features do not encode emotion identity in these models"; it does not support a claim about all possible spectral resolutions. Soften to match `user-model-paper/paper/main.tex:355`.

### 19. MINOR — The "mandatory control" conflates absence of evidence with evidence of absence

The robustness rule is "significant ($p < 0.05$) in $\geq 2$ of 3 categories" — uncorrected, against a Bonferroni-corrected α of 0.000625 for the overall test. At n ≈ 65 per category, p < 0.05 requires |ρ| ≥ 0.245. `Mistral Val × norm/token` (−0.24, −0.13, −0.04) is ruled "Ecological" partly on a coefficient sitting on the detection threshold. Some of the 19 "ecological artifacts" may be power loss.

**Fix:** report within-category CIs rather than significance verdicts, or state the minimum detectable |ρ| at n≈65 alongside the rule, and re-label the verdict column "Not robust at n≈65" rather than "Ecological."

## What I could NOT check, and what I need

**The entire twin-edition comparison.** You supplied one edition and marked the twin `[NOT PROVIDED]`. I could not check TWIN_DESYNC at all — not claim divergence, not number divergence, and not the structural defect you flagged (a row filed under a different in-table group label). Two things make this the highest-value gap: the paper carries a **retracted-finding correction**, which is exactly the case where the 2026-09-01 defect occurred; and this paper is **not in the `PAPERS` list of your own checker** at `tools/agni/twin_row_position.py:29-34`, so it has never been machine-checked. **Need:** `<paper>/main.tex` and `<paper>/academic/main.tex`. Then run `python tools/agni/twin_row_position.py --selftest` first (a clean result means nothing without the positive control) and add the paper to `PAPERS`.

**Whether the correction footnote exists in both editions.** Finding 6's fix is worthless if the note lives only in the integrity edition and the academic one ships the uncorrected text. Same files needed.

**Every number in Tables 1–5, the PCA variances, the std values, the parse rates, and N per model.** The underlying ratings and geometry are not in this repo. I checked `spectral-shape-paper/data/{Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct,Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct,Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3}_cognitive_states.json` — same three models, but the keys are confabulation-detection features (`mp_signal_rank`, `stable_rank`, …) with no self-report dimensions. Wrong dataset. **Need:** the analysis script and the per-trial ratings + delta features.

**STALE_PDF.** Cannot compare `main.pdf` mtime against `main.tex`. **Need:** both files, or `git log -1 --format=%ci` on each.

**The bibliography.** `watson2025interiora`, `wilterson2021attention`, `farrell2024attention`, and `mckenzie2026endogenous` appear **nowhere in this repository** — not in any `references.bib`, not in any `.tex`. I cannot check them for orphaned entries, missing entries, fabricated author names, or dead URLs. Two deserve specific scrutiny when you have the bib: `farrell2024attention` (attention schemas in transformer agents — the work I'm aware of in that space is Liu/Bolotta et al., arXiv 2305.17375; a "Farrell 2024" attribution needs a DOI or arXiv id confirming it) and `mckenzie2026endogenous` (activation-steering resistance). `graziano2017attention` I did verify — `presence-metric/references.bib:118`, DOI `10.3389/frobt.2017.00060`, correct.

**Author sign-off.** Four named authors including two external (Nell Watson, IEEE/Sentient Futures; Dwayne Wilkes, Sentient Futures). I have no way to see sign-off records. One inconsistency I can see: Wilkes's affiliation is ordered "Liberation Labs / Sentient Futures" here and "Sentient Futures / Liberation Labs" in `meta-pattern/main.tex:32`. Confirm which is primary and make it consistent.

**§3.1's forward reference to "Limitations."** The text I received ends mid-footnote — no Limitations section, no `\bibliography`, no `\end{document}`. Almost certainly paste truncation, but I cannot confirm the section that §3.1 promises ("the resulting selection bias is addressed in Limitations") actually exists. When you send the file, also make that reference a `\Cref{sec:limitations}` rather than prose, so it fails loudly at build time instead of rotting quietly.
